# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Iteration 1/5 · candidate `cand_0001` · parent: seed (EMPTY capability) · val baseline 0.350 (14/40)**

The seed was a genuine **no-skill control**: `prompt.md` existed but was empty, so
`_read_system_prompt` returned `""` and **no system message was sent at all**; `task_template.md`
was absent, so the adapter's built-in `_TASK_TEMPLATE` was used. I therefore CREATED both files.
The built-in template contained the line the brief warned about — *"Final solution code that writes
the modified file to output_path — once that file exists, you are done"* — and had no verification
round, which is exactly why 24/26 failures were never noticed by the agent itself.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × score recoverable, biggest first)

| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **A · Formula written instead of a literal value** | 25 of 26 failing: 267-18, 2768, 37378, 37456, 39046, 43436, 45635, 46897, 48588, 48620, 48921, 50768, 53383, 53647, 54144, 55049, 55979, 56563, 59196, 59595, 7902, 8942, 9569, 9726, 12864 | Primary metric is `hard_no_recalc`: the grader does `load_workbook(data_only=True)` and reads stored values. openpyxl saves a formula with **no cached result**, so the cell reads back `None`. The instructions literally say *"I need a formula…"*, so the agent complied correctly and scored 0. Sub-case: formulas **already present** in the answer cells also lose their cache on save (267-18, 48620, 54144, 9726). | KNOWLEDGE | add a sourced rule + tighten the output contract (skill §1, §4, §8) |
| 2 | **B · Blanket-overwriting the whole `answer_position` rectangle** | 48588 (17 cells), 50768 (7 + 6 blanks), 54144 (4), 48620 (4), 59196 (1) | `answer_position` is the *checked* range, not a box to fill. Cells already holding the right value (the user's hand-done worked example) and cells whose answer is genuinely blank must be left alone. | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL | add a rule + make "print the pre-filled cells first" an ordered step (skill §4, §6) |
| 3 | **C · No verification, no inspection — effectively single-shot** | all 26 (median 3 of 30 rounds used; 59196 and 51-12 did **zero** inspection rounds) | The built-in template declared the agent done as soon as the file existed, so nothing ever re-read the output. 3 of 4 non-formula failures had the ground truth sitting in the sheet (59196 `H3='D'`; 43436 header *"Open by end of May"* + example `H2=COUNTIFS(...,D:D,"")`; 51-12 row-2 markers `1,2,3,4`) and none were read. | BEHAVIORAL | ordered procedure + mandatory CHECK round as the definition of "done" (skill §6) |
| 4 | **D · Wrong type for a right answer** | 12864, 59196, 54144, 56563, 9726, 48588 | After rounding to 2dp the scorer requires `type(v1) == type(v2)`. Text written as a number, or a date written as a string, fails. (All 6 are also cluster A, so A's fix is a precondition for seeing D at all.) | KNOWLEDGE | explicit type table (skill §8) |
| 5 | **E · Loose prose outranked by in-sheet spec** | 43436 (counted "open during the month" instead of "open at end of month"; header said so) , 59196 (anchored `$D$1:$G$1` on an empty row 1 — headers are in row 2, misread from the pandas preview) | The instruction is a loose paraphrase; the column header and the user's neighbouring example formula are the real spec. | KNOWLEDGE | add a precedence rule + the `Unnamed:` header-row warning |
| 6 | **F · Float threshold comparison** | 51-12 (only pure-computation failure; `val >= ref*1.10` missed exact 10% steps because `100*1.10 == 110.00000000000001`; got 2 instead of 4) | Classic numeric trap in percentage/threshold tasks. | KNOWLEDGE | one-line rule with the integer-scaling fix |

**No ENVIRONMENT fault found.** Failures are content-specific and the grader behaved consistently;
463-17 hit a 60-second execution timeout but that was the agent's own auto-vivification infinite
loop (`ws[f"A{row}"]` grows `max_row`), and it recovered and passed. I folded that trap into the
recovery guidance rather than treating it as infrastructure.

## Changes made this iteration

| cluster | edit class (skill §) | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | add a sourced rule + add the reason (§4, §2) | `prompt.md` Rule 1 | States the grading mechanism (`data_only=True`, no recalc, openpyxl writes no cache) and the general policy "a named method is a preference, the value is the deliverable". No task id, value or answer appears. | Yes — 0/14 passing tasks write a formula as their graded answer |
| A (sub) | add a sourced rule (§4) | `prompt.md` Rule 1.2–1.3 | A formula *already in* an answer cell also loses its cache; recover its value via a second `data_only=True` load. Deliberately phrased as "decide what the cell should contain… if the instruction says blank, follow the instruction" so it cannot force a value into a cell meant to be cleared. | Yes — see 382-10 note below |
| D | tighten the output contract (§8) | `prompt.md` Rule 2 | A 4-row type table (number / date / text / nothing) read straight off the scorer's `transform_value` + `type(v1) != type(v2)`. | Yes |
| B | add a sourced rule (§4) | `prompt.md` Rule 3 | "`answer_position` is checked, not a box to fill": don't blanket-overwrite, pre-filled cells are a worked example, blank stays blank. | Yes, after rewording — see blast radius |
| — | add a sourced rule (§4) | `prompt.md` Rule 4 | Sheet resolution: quoted prefix, lopsided quotes, and **no prefix ⇒ `wb.sheetnames[0]`, not `wb.active`** (read directly off `compare_workbooks`). | Yes — 0/14 use `wb.active` |
| — | add a sourced rule (§4) | `prompt.md` Rule 5 | Ban the pandas writers only; openpyxl/zipfile both allowed. | Yes, after rewording |
| E, F | add a sourced rule + add the reason (§4, §2) | `prompt.md` Working style | Header/example precedence over loose prose; float-threshold scaling. | Yes |
| C | **ordered procedure + restructure** (§6) | `task_template.md` | Replaced the 2-step contract with READ → SOLVE → **CHECK**, and deleted *"once that file exists, you are done"*, replacing it with "You are done when the Round-3 output is all-clear". | Yes — turn headroom is large (max observed 6/30) |
| C | **worked example** (§5) | `task_template.md` Round 3 | A copyable, self-asserting check that mechanically catches cluster A (`assert not formulas`) and cluster B (`changed` vs input). Prose asking the agent to "be careful" would not have caught either. | Yes, after bounding — see below |
| A, B, E | restructure (§6) | `task_template.md` field semantics | Per-field meaning, the pandas-preview row/column offset (`preview row i == Excel row i+2`), the all-`Unnamed:` header-row warning, and the two-load (`ws` / `wsv`) idiom. | Yes |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)

- **A** — trace `2768`/`37378`/`46897`/`9569` etc. write e.g. `ws[f"A{row}"] = '=IF(B{row}<>"",COUNTA(...),"")'`; feedback: *"the grader reads the values saved in the file and does not recalculate… compute the result in Python and write the literal value instead."* Confirmed against source, not just the message: `adapter.py` `REWARD_RECALC` defaults to `0`, and `evaluation.py::compare_workbooks` does `load_workbook(proc_file, data_only=True)` → an openpyxl-written formula has no `<v>` and reads `None`. With Rule 1 present the agent computes the value in Python and assigns a literal. All 14 passing tasks already write literals, so none changes.
- **A (sub)** — trace `267-18` *modified the existing formula text* in `G1:G2` (`formula.replace('CONCATENATE("[",', ...)`), and `48620`/`54144`/`9726` left or replaced input formulas; all read back empty. Rule 1.2 makes the agent write the concatenated string / looked-up value literally instead.
- **A (verified by subagent against the saved artifacts)** — the 6 tasks whose feedback said *"Excel error text (e.g. #N/A)"* are the **same** cluster, not a separate one: none wrote an `"#N/A"` literal and none used `data_only=True`. They wrote post-2007 functions bare (`AGGREGATE`, `UNIQUE`, `TEXTJOIN`, `FILTER`, `TEXTSPLIT`, `MAXIFS`), which the xlsx grammar requires as `_xlfn.*`; the LibreOffice recalc used for the diagnostic note resolved them to `#NAME?`/`#VALUE!`. Writing literal values removes both the primary-metric failure and this one. I did **not** add an `_xlfn.` rule — it would only help a formula-based answer, which Rule 1 forbids.
- **D** — `12864` wrote a number where `str` was expected; `9726` a string where `datetime` was expected. Checked against the scorer, not the prompt: `transform_value` rounds numbers to 2dp and coerces numeric-looking strings, then `compare_cell_value` rejects on `type(v1) != type(v2)`; `("" , None)` is explicitly treated as equal, which is why the table says `None` *or* `""` is fine for blank.
- **B** — `48588`'s own inspection round printed `B2:B18 = 1,2,3,…` already filled and only `B19:B43` empty, then it overwrote all 42; golden `B2:B18` == input. `50768` filled all 9 matrix boxes when only 3 are non-empty in golden and `F14` was already correct. Rule 3 tells the agent to reproduce-then-continue, and CHECK item 3 surfaces an over-wide `changed` list.
- **C** — the old template said *"once that file exists, you are done"*; every failing trace stopped 1 round after saving (median 3 of 30 rounds). The new contract makes the Round-3 readback the **definition** of done, so the skipped step is a precondition of finishing rather than advice. Verified the step is load-bearing, not decorative: I ran the Round-3 snippet's logic against fixtures and it flags a leftover formula on both range shapes (`B2:B12` → `['B4']`, single cell `B4` → `['B4']`) while correctly **excluding** untouched example cells from `changed`.
- **E** — `59196` anchored `INDEX($D$1:$G$1, …)` on the empty row 1 (headers are in row 2, misread from an all-`Unnamed:` pandas preview) and overwrote `H3`, which already held the correct `'D'`. `43436` ignored the header *"Open by of end of May 2022"* and its own neighbouring example `H2=COUNTIFS(B:B,G2,D:D,"")`, counting records closed mid-month → 5 cells uniformly higher. Both edits are stated as general precedence rules; neither names a task or an expected value.
- **F** — `51-12` wrote the literal `2`, golden `4`; the subagent traced it to `100*1.10 == 110.00000000000001` rejecting the exact 10% steps, which then derailed the restart chain. The integer-scaling rule is general to percentage/threshold counting.
- **Template contract (mechanical)** — reproduced the adapter's own validator: comment stripped, all 6 required placeholders present, `max_turns` present, **0 unknown** placeholders, `str.format` renders, and all 4 embedded python blocks `compile()` cleanly with braces correctly doubled. A broken contract would have scored every task 0, so this was checked before anything else.

## Blast radius — stated per edit, and the three rules I reworded because of it

Creating a capability from nothing is unavoidably a **WIDE** change (every trajectory shifts), so
instead of claiming boundedness I ran a dedicated read-only audit of all 14 passing traces against
each drafted rule. It caught **three real regressions**, which I verified myself before rewording:

1. **80-42 would have broken.** It passes *because* it writes the literal strings `"None"` (cols D–I)
   and `"N/A"` (col J) into the graded range, matching the convention of the ~1000 existing rows.
   My first draft said *"never write a placeholder such as `0`, `"-"`, `"N/A"`"* — a deterministic
   regression on ~7000 cells. **Reworded** to: don't *invent* a filler, but match a convention the
   neighbouring rows of the same table already use.
2. **382-10 was at risk.** It must clear `A18`, which holds `=IFERROR(#REF!/#REF!,0)`, to `None`;
   the instruction never names A18. A flat "replace a formula with its computed value" could have
   written `0` there, and a flat "cells the instruction doesn't name keep their original value"
   could have stopped the clear. **Reworded** both: the formula rule defers to the instruction when
   the cell should end up blank, and Rule 3 permits clearing when *the instruction's rule applied
   uniformly* reaches the cell.
3. **463-17 and 6698 were at risk.** Both pass by writing the xlsx through `zipfile`/XML surgery
   (463-17 after its openpyxl attempt timed out). My first draft mandated "edit the loaded openpyxl
   workbook and save it". **Reworded** to ban only `DataFrame.to_excel`/`pd.ExcelWriter` and to
   allow XML surgery as an explicit fallback.
4. **80-42 and 402-43/395-36 printing/timeout risk.** 80-42's `answer_position` is
   `'Consolidate_ALL'!A2:L8000` = **95,988 cells**; my first CHECK snippet walked and printed all of
   them, which auto-vivifies cells and risks the 60-second block limit on a *passing* task. Rewrote
   it to use `range_boundaries` + a clip to `chk.max_row` and to slice every printout; verified by
   simulation that this reduces 80-42 to 12,012 cells (rows 2–1002) while leaving `B2:B12`, `B4`,
   `G12:J15` and `AO9:AO1288` exact.
5. **6698** changes method (literal int instead of formula + hand-patched cached `<v>`) but not
   graded content — the cached number it patched in came from its own Python count, which is the
   same integer Rule 1 has it write. Net simplification; it also removes two wasted rounds.
6. **560-12** clears `I2:J7` first; those cells are originally empty (data extent is A–D), so the
   clear is a no-op either way. Its explicit "left align, no other formatting" work is preserved by
   the carve-out in Rule 2 ("when the instruction explicitly asks for formatting, carry that out").

## Process & features used

- **Subagents (3, in parallel, read-only):** (1) mechanism of the `#N/A` cluster — it went to the
  saved `.norecalc`/recalc artifacts and proved these are the same formula cluster via the missing
  `_xlfn.` prefix, which I would not have found from the traces alone; (2) root cause of the 4
  non-formula failures (12864, 59196, 43436, 51-12); (3) the passing-trace regression audit, which
  is what caught the three rewordings above. The audit was the highest-value of the three — it
  turned a candidate that would have regressed 80-42 into one that should not.
- **Grounding in source rather than feedback text:** read `adapter.py` (`REWARD_RECALC`,
  `_read_system_prompt`, `_task_template_error`, `_TASK_TEMPLATE`) and
  `third_party/spreadsheetbench/evaluation/evaluation.py` (`transform_value`,
  `compare_cell_value`, `cell_level_compare`, `compare_workbooks`) so every contract claim is
  checked against what the scorer actually does. That is where the `sheetnames[0]`, the 2-decimal
  rounding, the `("" , None)` equivalence and the "formatting is not compared" facts came from.
- **Prior iterations:** none exist (`RUNMAP.md`/`LEDGER.md` empty, `rejected.jsonl` absent). I did
  read the repo's prior *experiment* champion for this benchmark
  (`docs/experiments/2026-09-26-spreadsheetbench-full_verified-gemma-4-31b/champion/task_template.md`)
  as reference material; it independently confirms the ordered READ/DECIDE/SOLVE/CHECK shape and the
  "named method is a preference" framing. I did **not** copy it: it was tuned for a much weaker
  reader (gemma-4-31b), it under-states the single fact that decides 25 of my 26 failures (it says
  "graded only on resulting cell values" but never that the grader does not recalculate), and three
  of its rules are the exact ones my passing-trace audit flagged as regressions here.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)

- **Rule 1 is the whole iteration.** 25 of 26 failures are formula-instead-of-value. Do not soften
  it, and do not "allow a formula as long as it's also given a cached value" — the primary metric
  reads the file as saved.
- **The deleted line.** Never restore *"once that file exists, you are done"*. The Round-3 CHECK
  being the definition of done is the structural fix for cluster C.
- **The three rewordings in §Blast radius.** They are not stylistic: the blunt versions regress
  80-42, 382-10, and 463-17/6698. Re-read that section before tightening any of those rules.
- **The clip to `chk.max_row`** in the CHECK snippet — without it 80-42 walks 95,988 cells.

## Deliberately skipped

- **`_xlfn.` prefixing for post-2007 functions** — real and verified, but it only helps an answer
  that *is* a formula, which Rule 1 forbids. Adding it would compete with Rule 1 and invite the
  agent back onto the losing path.
- **Whole-column vs bounded ranges (`INDEX($B:$B,…)` recalculating text to `0`, 12864)** — a
  property of the LibreOffice recalc path, not of the primary metric. Moot once literals are written.
- **Per-task reasoning fixes for 43436 and 51-12** — these two need correct reasoning, not a
  missing fact. I shipped only the *generalizable* lesson behind each (in-sheet header/example
  outranks loose prose; don't compare floats against a scaled threshold) and no task specifics.
- **Nothing was skipped for lack of time.** All six clusters got an edit.
